swap.evidence: Swapped products: a neighbourhood seed library and a community-hall room booking. Surviving unchanged: the masthead (generic icon + name in bold body text), the H1 + lede + search + uniform card grid, the placeholder-square thumbnails, the green chip, the check-and-confirm form, the bordered done box. Bound to this product: the session calendar with 'Open' days, the deposit in every card's meta line, and the copy ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'the previous borrower', 'call the desk'). With the name hidden, a reader can tell it is for borrowing things at set sessions only from the copy, not from anything visual.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a small community lending/booking service: pale neutral ground, white bordered cards in a grid, one muted green accent, a friendly sans, GOV.UK-style forms and error summary, icon placeholders where photos would go. Predicted opposite: a warm handmade/craft look (kraft paper, stamped labels, hand-drawn type). The design matches the default on ground, card grid, accent, type and form pattern; it avoids the opposite. Only the 'Open' session tags are not predicted by either.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'reservation flow for a toy library run by parents in a church hall, open two mornings a week'. Predicted choices: search + card grid with availability chips, a date picker marking open days, radio session cards, a confirm form, a plain confirmation table. Overlap: nearly total; the only brief-driven differences are the deposit line and the tool-spec copy.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Zero detector hits on a page with ten identical placeholder thumbnails is surprising; either the stand-in rule (SLP-58) is judgement-only or the detector section was not populated for this run. My verdicts are unchanged.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: On find, all ten cards carry an identical pale-green square with the same wrench glyph where a picture of the tool would go. It carries no information (a drill, a ladder and a pressure washer look the same) and reads as an unfinished placeholder in the first viewport at every width and theme.
findings.impact: Members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' may have to read every title because the thumbnails give no visual cue; the page is likely to look unfinished to first-time members.

evidence.detail: ten identical thumbnail squares at x=113 and x=665

findings.recommendation: Decide what each card's image slot is for: real photos of the library's own tools, or remove the slot and let the name and spec carry the card. Do not keep a repeated stand-in.

findings.title: No identity or focal element of the library's own on find, basket, confirm and done
findings.description: Apart from the copy and the tool page's 'Open' calendar tags, nothing visual belongs to Fernhill: the name is set in bold body text beside a generic wrench glyph, the ground is a neutral pale grey-green, there is no imagery of the community centre, the membership card or the tools, and no page has a focal element beyond its H1. Swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests all fail for the frame.
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' is carried only by the copy; members may not recognise the page as their library's, and the flow is likely to feel like a generic form rather than the desk they know.
findings.recommendation: Decide the identity floor from the library's own world named in DESIGN.md (the membership card, the room, the desk) and carry it through the masthead and one element per page, without adding hero moments to Operate surfaces.

findings.title: At 375 the search field sits below all ten tool cards on find
findings.description: At 1280 the search field follows the lede; at 375 (and in no-results/375) it is moved after the whole card list, about 1,600 px down, just above Opening times.
findings.impact: Most members use phones; the surface's job is 'find a tool' and the tool for it may be missed or need a long scroll, and the order differs from desktop.
findings.recommendation: Keep the search and filter in the same reading position at every width.

findings.title: Tool names truncate at 375 so the two cordless drills read identically
findings.description: Card titles are cut to one line with an ellipsis at 375: 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' appears twice, hiding 'two batteries' vs 'one battery'; 'Extension ladder 3 m …', 'Pressure washer, 130 …' lose their key spec.
findings.impact: The distinguishing spec members use ('the drill with two batteries') is exactly what is hidden, so a member may open the wrong tool.
findings.recommendation: Let tool names wrap on narrow cards; decide how the card shares width between thumbnail and name at 375.

findings.title: Dark theme: 'available' chips lose their ground while 'later' chips keep one
findings.description: In dark mode the green 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' chips show as bare green text (the selection ground is nearly the card colour), while the grey 'Available from Sat 17 Oct / Wed 21 Oct / Sat 24 Oct' chips keep a visible grey ground. The soon-available state ends up visually weaker than the later one, the opposite of light mode.
findings.impact: Members in dark mode (common in the evening use scene) may read the later-availability tools as the highlighted ones.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark chip pair so the available state keeps at least the emphasis it has in light mode.

findings.title: Basket session options split 1 + 5 with dates wrapping to three lines
findings.description: At 1280 the six session radio cards render as one full-width card (Wed 28 Oct) followed by five narrow cards in a row whose labels wrap to three lines ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00'). They are also listed latest first, so the earliest session sits last at the far right.
findings.impact: The one choice this page exists for looks broken and is harder to scan; members looking for 'Saturday morning' may have to read six wrapped labels in reverse date order.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list at each width that keeps every label on one or two lines, in date order.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unstyled native date and select controls, misaligned
findings.description: The opened filter shows a browser-default 'yyyy/mm/dd' date input and a native select with a small default chevron; the 'Category' label and select sit about 30 px lower than 'Available from' and its input because the hint text pushes the first column.
findings.impact: The only unthemed controls in the product make the filter look unfinished, and the yyyy/mm/dd format contradicts the en-GB 'Saturday 17 October' format used everywhere else.
findings.recommendation: Bring the filter controls into the same input system as the rest of the flow (44 px, the loan-length select's style) and align the two fields on a shared top line.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different label-column widths
findings.description: On the tool page the Details list is split: Category/Deposit/Available from align values at x≈224, while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case align values at x≈180, so the list zig-zags.
findings.impact: Small, but it undercuts 'careful' on the page where members compare specs; the eye has to re-find the value column halfway down.
findings.recommendation: Align both groups on one value column, or separate them visibly as two lists.

findings.title: Footer band stops short, leaving an empty grey band on short pages
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280 the white footer band ends mid-viewport and the page ground continues below it for 100-200 px.
findings.impact: The confirmation page, the last thing a member sees, looks unfinished at its end.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages end: the footer reaching the viewport bottom or the ground matching the footer.

strengths: The copy voice: concrete, friendly, volunteer-desk tone ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower').
One filled button per page in one green, so the primary action is never in doubt.
The pick-up calendar tags session days 'Open', the one visual device taken from how the library actually works.
Error summary with linked messages and example-bearing hints in both themes.
keep: Keep the volunteer-desk copy and the single-filled-button rule; any identity work must not dilute either.
not_assessable: Motion (toast fade, button colour), focus rings, sticky action bar and toast placement in a real viewport (full-page captures draw the fixed bar and toast mid-page), calendar keyboard behaviour.
No baseline screenshots in the packet, so DES-05 pairwise is not applicable.
notes: Isolated subagent. Did not read source, builder notes or other critics' output. Verdicts written to critic-1.verdict.json before unsealing; detectors returned 0 hits. No baseline, pairwise not run.
